content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1770937805.214409\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"hey, one thing before the next BoomBit sync. Once the data export is done Slack drops to the free plan and the history goes, and most of DD's bug tracking since the Unity 6 move only lives in there, Vincent's Android canvas and whatever came in after it. Linear stays through the transition, so I want the whole list moved over, the fixed ones too, that's the only record of what was done. I put you back on one of the paid seats so you can read the DD channels for this. How we call each one is in the carry-over notes doc I shared with you. content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"title\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"revisionId\": \"42599f1a8a\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\"}"}

An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.
"}

This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.
1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes
When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):
• UI is rendered *by a Camera*
• It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*
• Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path
• On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:
Not render at all, or
Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)
This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.

2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency
When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.
In other words:
> Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*.
3. Why this happens only on some Android devices
Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes
Key Takeaway
The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:
> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*

The Gist
Team discusses upcoming projects, sales tax, game mechanics, gold tiles, rewind button, dynamite tiles, workload, and goals to ensure successful completion of projects and avoid burnout.

Action Items
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to check if sales tax is charged for subscription software purchases
• Arthur to check if sales tax is charged for Figma subscription
• Arthur to run Unity seat licenses through [PERSON_NAME_0054]’ card to avoid sales tax
• Leonard to break down Figma pages into multiple pages for easier navigation
• Arthur to close out the family and friends build by the end of the day
• Leonard to aim for the end of the first week of October for the next family and friends build
• Arthur to create tickets for various tasks related to the family and friends build
• [PERSON_NAME_0029] to limit the wildcard to one per row in the game
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to make a minor change to the game rules to allow for either one wildcard or one redemption tile per row, or one of each.
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to clarify the logic behind the calculation of the number of tiles per row.
• Leonard to adjust the percentage for gold tiles to increase the number of goals.
• [PERSON_NAME_0029] to share the details about how things are calculated with [PERSON_NAME_0054].
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to focus on low-hanging fruit tasks and not work on the rewind feature.
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to hide the rewind button for the family and friends build.
• Arthur to help [PERSON_NAME_0099] figure out how to handle the collision issue with dynamite tiles.
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to try flagging the tiles affected by dynamite explosions and figure out how to handle the collision issue.
• [PERSON_NAME_0099] to fix the bug found by [PERSON_NAME_97912] [PERSON_NAME_0099] to work on the rewind feature and address the issues with the bomb tile
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to test the rewind feature and its impact on streak bonuses
• Leonard to gather feedback from the team on the additional stress and workload caused by the family and friends build Push
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to discuss with [PERSON_NAME_5466] on how to assess scenarios like the friends and family build
• Leonard to ensure functional aspects of the friends and family build meet the quality bar
• Leonard to provide a better context and set expectations before starting a project
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] and Leonard to deliver an even better version of the build by the upcoming Friday
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to have a conversation with the team about overworking and the potential risks of burnout
• Leonard to encourage team members to take vacations and have conversations about workload management
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to share his experiences with managing individuals who struggle with workload management
• Leonard to take more vacations and encourage others to do the same
• Team to have conversations about workload planning and overcommunication to prevent overdrives
• [PERSON_NAME_0054] to thank the team for their input and feedback during the postmortem meeting
Status Update By Topic
• Sales Tax: Discussed the possibility of sales tax being charged for subscription software and physical goods, with [PERSON_NAME_0054] noting that he can buy things for the company to avoid sales tax.
• Wildcard Tiles: Discussed the current restriction of one wildcard or redemption tile per row, with [PERSON_NAME_0054] proposing a change to allow one wildcard and one redemption tile per row.
• Family and Friends Build: Agreed to aim for the end of the first week of October to have the build ready for the board meeting.
• Ticket Creation: Agreed to create tickets for the family and friends stuff, with Arthur noting that they need to close it out today.
• Glow Effect: Discussed the glow effect for pieces revealed via wildcard, with Leonard noting that it was nice to have but not a priority.
• Darkening Water: Discussed the mini game darkening water, with Leonard noting that it was hard to see on the iPhone.
• Bill Check: Discussed checking the bill from today, with Arthur noting that they built up a few hours ago.
• Calculation Logic: The team discussed the logic behind the calculation of the number of tiles per row. They determined that it is not a simple 25% equal chance per number, as the probability of rolling a seven on two dice is higher than rolling ones and twelves.
• UI: [PERSON_NAME_0029] is working on the UI part for the shop, and [PERSON_NAME_0099] is focusing on the long hair, low hanging fruits upon attack, take rewind. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested hiding the rewind button for the family and friends build.
• Dynamite Tiles: Dynamite tiles are causing issues as they are competing to remove the same piece off the board. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested flagging them or setting a state to sort through the affected tiles. [PERSON_NAME_0099] is working on the bug and will try [PERSON_NAME_5466]’s suggestion.
• Rewind: Rewind is proving to be difficult as it requires a lot of things to be done. [PERSON_NAME_5466] suggested flagging or setting a state to mark the affected tiles. [PERSON_NAME_0099] is working on the bug and will try [PERSON_NAME_5466]’s suggestion.
• Rewind Feature: The team discussed the edge cases and stipulations of the rewind feature, such as the wild card bonus in Domino Dreams, and the fact that rewinding the last piece does not remove the streak effect.
• Family and Friends Build Push: The team discussed the impact of the Push on the engineering team, and the importance of setting clear goals and timelines to avoid overworking and cramming new things at the last minute.
• Optimization: The team discussed the need to set aside time for optimization and tuning when introducing new assets.
• Silver Bullet Philosophy: The team discussed the importance of understanding the true importance of a goal to the business and how to articulate it to the team.
• Asian Engineering: The team discussed the common experience of [NATIONALITY_2601] engineers not communicating their struggles and how to manage their workload.
• Quality Bar: The team discussed the importance of setting a quality bar for the work and how to ensure it is met.
• Overdrive: The team discussed the importance of avoiding overdrive and burnout and how to manage workloads.
• Vacations: The team discussed the importance of taking vacations and how to encourage it.

Dataset
• *18 lost attempts* (App versions: *1.0.56 = 15*, *1.0.57 = 3*)
• All rows have the key gameplay fields populated.
Do losers buy pieces?
Yes, always.
*18/18 (100%)* bought pieces.
• Pieces bought distribution: *median 7*, p25 *5.25*, p75 *9*, range *2–12*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t buying” is not the issue.

Do losers sell pieces?
Rarely (for actual tiles).
• *Tiles Sold Int > 0:* *6/18 (33%)*
Tiles sold: median *0*, p75 *1*, max *9*.
• *Trash Sold Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
Trash sold: median *8*, range *2–18*.
Takeaway: if “selling tiles” is a core mechanic, adoption is low. Trash selling looks universal, so either it is easy/automatic, or it is the only “sell” behavior players understand.

Do losers remove obstacles?
Yes, always.
*Obstacles Removed Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
• Obstacles removed: *median 4*, p75 *6*, range *1–7*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t removing obstacles” is not supported by this dataset.

Do losers build combos?
You still do not log combos directly, but *Highest Dps Int* is your best proxy.
• Highest DPS: *median 508.5*, p75 *621*, max *1189*.
Takeaway: many losing runs ramp to substantial DPS, especially in late deaths, so a large part of the problem is not “no combos,” it is “combos not enough to survive the late curve” or “spend not converting to survivability.”

What does Silver Balance Int tell us?
Everyone dies with silver left.
• *Silver Balance Int*: median *84*, p75 *108*, max *160*, min *38*.
Takeaway: players are not ending at “0 resources.” They are dying with spendable currency still in hand, which usually points to one of:
1. spend options are not impactful enough to change outcomes,
2. shop decisions are unclear (players buy the wrong things),
3. shop timing/UX friction (they do not spend at the right moment).
How behavior changes by where they die
Segmented by *Highest Wave Reached Int*:
Early deaths (<= 6), N=4
Pieces bought median *4.5*
Obstacles removed median *2*
DPS median *178*
Silver median *67*
• Tiles sold any *25%*
Interpretation: these are “didn’t ramp” runs, likely skill/understanding + early variance.
Mid deaths (7–9), N=4
Pieces bought median *6*
Obstacles removed median *4.5*
DPS median *376.5*
Silver median *71*
• Tiles sold any *50%* (highest of the three groups)
Interpretation: midgame wall starts showing, some players try selling as a recovery move.
Late deaths (>= 10), N=10
Pieces bought median *9*
Obstacles removed median *5.5*
DPS median *611*
Silver median *107*
• Tiles sold any *30%*
Interpretation: late losers are actively playing the systems (buying, clearing, ramping DPS) and still die, often with meaningful silver left. That is tuning plus spend-impact, not “they didn’t engage.”

What you should change (based on this)
If you want win rate to move hard, focus on two things.
1) Make spending convert into survival
You have clear evidence of “dies with silver left,” especially in late runs.
Add *recommended purchase* (one button) when HP is low or wave >= 10 and silver >= X.
• Add *auto-open shop* at wave checkpoints (ex: after wave 6 and wave 10) with 1–2 highlighted options.
• Buff the best defensive/sustain option so it reliably prevents late deaths (shield, lifesteal, regen spike, damage reduction).
2) Decide whether tile-selling is supposed to matter
Because Tiles Sold is only *33%*:
• If selling is intended core: force it in FTUE once, and add a contextual prompt when the board is tight (“sell lowest value tile” preselected).
• If selling is optional: stop assuming it is the reason for losses, and tune the level assuming most players will not sell tiles.
One logging gap to close
To prove your theory cleanly, you need:
• *Silver spent total* and *purchase types* (offense vs defense vs utility), plus *time since last purchase*.
Right now you only know they _bought some pieces_ and _had silver left_. You cannot tell whether they failed because they did not spend, or because they spent on weak/wrong things.

A bad state FLag or race could leave the blocker on, so the player taps the start button but the click never reaches the Level-1 loader.   *Level-1 scene itself* _2b545068c2_ “*Fix level 1 being broken*” Indicates Level 1 was _actually failing to load_ sometime after the previous tag. If the scene threw an exception you’d still record the “first_open” but never the “begin_level 1”.   *Overlay panels on first run* _de5198034f_ “FPS don’t block clicks.” (fix) Tells us an overlay _was_ blocking clicks before this fix. If the fix went in _after_ 0.3.90 was cut, the shipped build might still have the blocker.   *Unlock / gating tweaks* _0defc0e873_ “Changing items screen unlock level from 4 to 5”_1c30ce07b3_ “Changing tutorials appearance order and names” Moving an FTUE popup earlier (or mis-ordering it) can halt progression before the Level-1 load.   *Splash / pre-load flow* _58121674b4_ “Fix splash progress. Disable FPS panel by default.” If splash progress never reaches “ready”, the player may quit before Level-1 is triggered.
Highest-leverage suspects
1. *Tutorial input-blocking refactor*
2.  The trio of commits around blocking/auto-closing tutorials is the most likely root cause. One misplaced `SetBlockInput(true)` that never flips back would cut the conversion rate exactly the way we’re seeing.
3. *Broken Level-1 scene (now fixed)*
4.  If _2b545068c2_ landed *after* the 0.3.90 branch was cut, the live build might crash or hang when trying to enter Level 1, giving you the same 13-point drop.
What to check next
   Check How     *Crash / exception logs for scene “Level1”* Firebase, GameAnalytics, or Unity’s Cloud Diagnostics on builds tagged 0.3.90. Look for `BeginLevel` fired without the matching `LevelLoaded` metric.   *Input-blocker state after first tutorial* QA a fresh install on 0.3.90 with Unity profiler _Input Debug_ window: verify `UIInputBlocker.IsActive == false` before the Level-1 button becomes tappable.   *Event timing* Query the time delta between `first_open` and the _first_ `begin_level` per user. A flat spike at ~10–20 s followed by a long tail suggests some users are stuck rather than churning.   *Compare internal vs. store build hashes* Make sure the fixes in _de5198034f_ and _2b545068c2_ actually made it into the binary you shipped to testers. It’s easy for a hot-fix to stay on `develop` while the release branch lags.
Quick mitigation
• Ship a hot-fix that *re-verts/guards the input-blocking logic* + *includes the Level-1 scene fix*.
• Add an analytics heartbeat that fires “*FTUE_blocked > 10 s*” if the blocker is still active 10 seconds after first open—gives you an early warning next time.

import json
recs=json.load(open('/tmp/recs.json'))
rows=[['Bug','Outcome','Ticket','Why']]
n=2438
for r in recs:
  if r['outcome']=='Covered': t='ENG-2363'
  else: t='ENG-%d'%n; n+=1
  rows.append([r['bug'],r['outcome'],t,r['why']])
print(n-1)
json.dump(rows,open('/tmp/rows.json','w'),ensure_ascii=False)
print(json.dumps(rows,ensure_ascii=False))
"

content.text:
I've done everything Arthur asked, following his carry-over notes doc, and replied in his DM thread with the numbers: **8 still broken, 69 new tickets, 25 of 28 UI children Done.**

**What went over (70 bugs)**
- **Canvas lines:** 63 from Vincent's "Bugs on Android 2231" canvas. Six more had their text deleted, so per the notes there was nothing to carry over.
- **Bug channel posts:** 7 from #god-bugs posted after the last canvas line. I left out the post pointing at a QA doc and the no-ads question for Leonard, since the notes say those aren't bug posts.
- **Outcomes:**
  - 59 Fixed (Done)
  - 3 Gone (Canceled): the lives bugs, because lives were removed from the game on Dec 3.
  - 1 Covered: the Android manual sign-in line. Vincent had already tied it to ENG-2363, so I added a note there with the canvas wording instead of filing a new ticket.
  - 7 Broken (Bugs)
- **Linear:** the 69 new tickets are ENG-2438 to ENG-2506. All are Engineering, Bug label, under ENG-2401, with no assignee or description. Each title starts with `[2231]` — Arthur asked for that in a comment on the master ticket after he wrote the doc.

**The 7 still broken, plus the covered one** (the four non-obvious ones first)
- **River Tile / Memory Tile shop icons:** the canvas line is ticked, but on Dec 1 Brian said the round icons were back ("don't trust that tick").
- **Tile dozer background:** the fix is in Marcus's PR #1913, which was never merged.
- **Megatile missing a face:** I found no fix commit after the report.
- **Train level backgrounds:** QA left it open after the last fix attempt.
- **The other three:** Apple sign-in, backend errors after losing a level, and the navigation bar disappearing after quitting a team.
- **Covered:** Android manual sign-in, tracked on ENG-2363.

**UI tree**
- 16 open children moved to Done.
- Left where they were:
  - Collect & Win: the screen is switched off in the build.
  - Season Pass: Oliver says the reward track still uses the old frames.
  - Daily Gift: Brian's last pass never landed.
- The doc says Brian's closing rule applies to the line on every child. I found that rule in a Trello comment: every close-out note names the current public build. So each child's line says where it landed and names 0.3.310. The three masters are unchanged.

**Sheet:** "DD bug carry-over" in your DD bug carry-over folder, with columns Bug / Outcome / Ticket / Why. It's shared read-only with Arthur, Robert and Oliver, the other people on the Sunday invite: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/7b929acb5cf6d85b/edit

**Judgement calls worth checking before Sunday**
- **Which code counts as the build:** the branch build 310 was made from (`Blake/boombitFixAddressables`) isn't on GitHub. Because the notes say 0.3.310 "came off the economy line", I treated everything on EconomyChanges as being in the build.
- **Robert's music bug:** I marked it Fixed based on your Dec 5 commit "Updated URLAudioPlayer to fully download clip if needed", which is the music player Brian pointed at. The commit doesn't name the bug, so this one is the least certain.
